title: Pointed rational cones admit integral defining inequalities spanning the dual
statement: Let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank, that is, an abelian group with a finite $\mathbf Z$-basis, and put $V=L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$, regarding $L\subseteq V$ by $\ell\mapsto\ell\otimes1$. Let $v_1,\ldots,v_m\in L$ (allowing $m=0$) and let $C=\{\sum_j q_jv_j:q_j\in\mathbf Q_{\ge0}\}\subseteq V$. Assume $C$ is pointed, $C\cap(-C)=\{0\}$, and spans $V$, every element of $V$ being a difference of two elements of $C$. Then there are an integer $r\ge0$ and group homomorphisms $\varphi_1,\ldots,\varphi_r:L\to\mathbf Z$ whose $\mathbf Q$-linear extensions $V\to\mathbf Q$ span $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q}(V,\mathbf Q)$ and such that $$C=\{v\in V:\varphi_i(v)\ge0\text{ for every }i\}.$$ When $V=0$ the empty family ($r=0$) works; when $V\neq0$ every such family has $r\ge1$.

source.place: Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103, points to the rational polyhedral fan description but does not state this lattice form. Kato 1994, Toric singularities, is WANTED for the integral dual-cone theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite] to $V=L\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and the given vectors $v_j$. It gives a finite family of rational linear forms $\lambda_i:V\to\mathbf Q$ with $C=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge0\ \text{for all }i\}$. If $V=0$, take the empty family and $r=0$; hence assume $V\ne0$.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103; Kato 1994 rational polyhedral-cone theorem (WANTED).

proof.text: Choose the given finite $\mathbf Z$-basis of $L$ and write each $\lambda_i$ in the associated dual basis with rational coefficients. Multiply $\lambda_i$ by a positive integer $d_i$ clearing all denominators, and set $\varphi_i=d_i\lambda_i$. Then $\varphi_i(L)\subseteq\mathbf Z$, so each $\varphi_i$ is an integral group homomorphism $L\to\mathbf Z$; multiplying an inequality by $d_i>0$ does not change its nonnegative locus, so $C=\{x:\varphi_i(x)\ge0\ \text{for all }i\}$. The rescaled forms span the same $\mathbf Q$-subspace as the $\lambda_i$.

source.place: Agent expansion of the lattice-coordinate step following Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.

proof.text: The forms $\varphi_i$ span $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Q}(V,\mathbf Q)$. Indeed, if $x\in V$ is annihilated by every $\varphi_i$, then both $x$ and $-x$ satisfy all the defining inequalities, hence $x\in C\cap(-C)=\{0\}$ by pointedness. Thus their common kernel is zero; in finite dimension this is equivalent to their linear span being the whole dual space (extend a basis of their span and use the nonzero coordinate functional on a complementary direction). Therefore the resulting finite family has the required spanning property. Since $V\ne0$, its dual is nonzero and a spanning family cannot be empty, so $r\ge1$.

lean.statement: theorem rationalConeDualIntegralForms (L : Type u) [AddCommGroup L] [Module.Free ℤ L] [Module.Finite ℤ L] (m : ℕ) (v : Fin m → L) : let V := ℚ ⊗[ℤ] L let C : Set V := {x | ∃ q : Fin m → ℚ≥0, x = ∑ j, (q j : ℚ) • TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (1 : ℚ) (v j)} (C ∩ (-C) = ({0} : Set V)) → (∀ x : V, ∃ c₁ ∈ C, ∃ c₂ ∈ C, x = c₁ - c₂) → (∃ (r : ℕ) (φ : Fin r → L →+ ℤ) (Φ : Fin r → V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ), (∀ (i : Fin r) (ℓ : L), Φ i (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (1 : ℚ) ℓ) = (φ i ℓ : ℚ)) ∧ Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range Φ) = ⊤ ∧ C = {x | ∀ i, 0 ≤ Φ i x} ∧ ((∀ x : V, x = 0) → r = 0)) ∧ ((∃ x : V, x ≠ 0) → ∀ (r : ℕ) (φ : Fin r → L →+ ℤ) (Φ : Fin r → V →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ), (∀ (i : Fin r) (ℓ : L), Φ i (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (1 : ℚ) ℓ) = (φ i ℓ : ℚ)) → Submodule.span ℚ (Set.range Φ) = ⊤ → C = {x | ∀ i, 0 ≤ Φ i x} → 0 < r)
